entry.title: SAP Community Voice: Joule Expert Tips, Petoberfest, Learning Stories and the Magic of Events!
entry.content:
Featured Blog Posts 

Enterprise AI development with SAP Joule Studio 

SAP Champion Prasad Khandavalli explores a new approach to enterprise AI development with SAP Joule Studio. His blog post explains how Joule Studio enables teams to start with a business outcome expressed in natural language and turn that intent into the requirements, development artifacts, testing, and agent capabilities needed to build AI-powered business solutions. The post also shows the different solution types available in Joule Studio, from AI agents and n8n workflows to data products and extensions, as well as how teams can move from no-code to pro-code development. 

Read Prasad Blog post here 

Your ABAP Backlog Is Not a Capacity Problem: AI for Consultants 

ABAP backlogs may not be a capacity problem after all.  SAP Community member Siarhei published a blog post on how the real bottleneck can be the gap between the person who understands a business requirement and the developer who implements it. Instead of focusing only on making developers faster, his team moved the AI toolchain to consultants, giving them access to business data, existing custom code, development tools, and the company’s own development rules. This allows consultants to work through a requirement from functional specification to technical specification, ABAP code, and testing while keeping the business context throughout the process. 

Read Siarhei Blog post here 

SAP SuccessFactors Solution Architecture Leading Practices for 2026/2027 

SAP SuccessFactors Architecture Leading Practices (ALPs) are being refreshed for 2026/2027, with the first updates now available. SAP expert Dayna Carnino introduces the updated guidance and explains what is covered across the latest ALPs, from deployment and rollout strategy to job architecture and Talent Intelligence Hub, People Analytics, and translation strategy. She also highlights why these decisions are important to address early in a SuccessFactors implementation, helping teams avoid rework and challenges later on. 

Read Dayna Blog post here 

Running Your Agents as Background Jobs with Agentic AI on BTP 

SAP Mentor Wouter Lemaire dives into how to turn an existing AI agent into a scheduled background job using the SAP BTP Job Scheduling Service. This makes it possible to automate recurring tasks such as daily system checks, overnight job analysis, transport overviews, and security note checks, without anyone having to manually prompt the agent. He also explains how scheduled runs can produce a structured report. If you would like to understand how to take an agent from “an agent I can ask”   to “an agent that tells me”  we highly recommend checking out Wouter’s latest blog post. 

Read Wouter Blog Post here

Community News 

Devtoberfest: coding, fun activities and pets!  

Devtoberfest 2026 brings the SAP developer community together for weeks of learning, coding, technical challenges, and collaboration. It is a chance to build new skills, try out SAP technologies, connect with fellow developers, and earn points along the way. And now, even your pets can join the experience! Petoberfest invites participants to share a picture of their pet, pet rock, chia pet, or stuffed animal companion, with 600 points awarded for an approved picture. Check out the blog post by SAP Developer Advocate Dan Wroblewski to find out all the details on how to participate. The Petoberfest 2026 gallery is already live here, so check out the adorable pets already shared by the community, and remember that Devtoberfest runs until October 18, so there is still time to get involved! 

SAP Certification Learning Stories!  

SAP Expert Margherita Gallucci from the SAP Learning team recently shared an inspiring learner story about Shivani Dwivedi and her SAP career journey. We would like to invite you to read Shivani’s story (blog post here) and feel inspired by how taking that first step, staying curious, and continuing to learn can become the beginning of a fulfilling journey with SAP. From discovering ABAP to earning certifications in ABAP Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud, SAP Build, and Generative AI, Shivani’s experience shows how learning can open new possibilities along the way.  And we would also like to remind you about the #MySAPCertificationStory initiative, celebrating 30 years of SAP Certification! Whether you earned your first certification decades ago or just this year, the SAP Learning team would love to hear the story behind your journey. Share your #MySAPCertificationStory by commenting on Margherita’s blog post and be part of the celebration! SAP Expert Margherita’s blog post here 

Events 

Get Ready for SAP TechEd in Berlin!  

A quick reminder that SAP TechEd Berlin is coming up on October 27–29!  It is a great opportunity to get hands-on with SAP’s latest technologies, learn how to build AI-powered systems, dive into technical sessions and workshops. The SAP Community Clubhouse and Developer Garage will also be there, giving you opportunities to meet SAP leaders, Mentors, Champions, and Developer Advocates in person. And if you are attending, do not miss the SAP Community Meetup on October 26, the evening before TechEd, at Hofbräuhaus Berlin from 6:00 p.m. There will be no presentations or formal agenda, just an evening to meet fellow SAP enthusiasts, reconnect with the community.  Registration is required, so sign up for the meetup here and register for SAP TechEd here. 

Reminder: SAP Inside Track Munich 10-Year Anniversary! 

A special milestone is coming up for the SAP community in Munich! This Saturday, October 10, SAP Inside Track Munich celebrates its 10th edition at SAP Labs Munich in Garching. After a decade of bringing the local community together, this anniversary edition is a great opportunity to spend the day learning, exchanging ideas, and connecting with fellow SAP professionals. The event runs from 9:00 to 18:00, with the agenda featuring a full day of community-driven sessions. And the celebrations start tomorrow! Friday, October 9 will happen a Learning Session from 10:00 to 16:00 at SAP in Garching, followed by the pre-evening meetup from 18:00 at Piacere Nuovo. Both are open for registration here. If you cannot make it tomorrow, there is still time to join the community on Saturday and celebrate 10 years of SAP Inside Track Munich! 

SAP community Events Magic  

Do you need a reason to attend an in-person SAP community event? SAP Community Manager Moshe Naveh might just inspire you! In his latest blog post (check here), Moshe shares his experience from a weekend filled with events in Porto, including SAP CodeJam and SAP Inside Track Porto. From hands-on learning and inspiring sessions to the conversations, questions, ideas, and connections that continued long after the presentations, Moshe highlights what makes being together in person so special. His experience is also a reminder that, while AI is changing the way we work and learn, there is still something special about bringing people together in person. Community events are an opportunity to meet others who are facing similar challenges and learning along the way, exchange ideas, have honest conversations, and connect with SAP Community Advocates and leaders beyond the screen!

Autonomous Enterprise

    Your Journey to the Autonomous Enterprise: Unlocking Value with SAP GROW and RISE with SAP

  • 20 жовтня, 17:00 – 17:45
    RISE with SAP: Building the Foundation for Agentic AI at Scale
    Чому модернізація ERP є ключовою передумовою для масштабного впровадження agentic AI та яку роль відіграє RISE with SAP у побудові цього фундаменту.

SAP Business AI Platform та Integration Suite

  • 13 жовтня, 16:00 – 17:00
    Secure, Compliant, and AI-Ready: The Future of Governance and Compliance on SAP BTP
    Як SAP BTP забезпечує regulatory compliance через анонімізацію даних, аудит-логи та AI-орієнтовані insights — мультігалузеве демо для архітекторів та команд безпеки.
  • 14 жовтня, 17:00 – 18:00
    Modernize from SAP Process Integration and SAP Process Orchestration
    Міграція з SAP PI/PO на SAP Integration Suite: підходи до переходу, варіанти співіснування та конкретні результати — швидші change-цикли і краща надійність.
  • 27 жовтня, 17:00 – 18:00
    SAP Integration Suite — Monthly Update October
    Щомісячне оновлення SAP Integration Suite: нові можливості, вдосконалення та інтерактивна сесія Q&A з Integration Black Belt.

SAP Cloud ERP та Transformation

  • 20 жовтня, 15:00 – 16:00
    Managing SAP Business Suite 7 Extended Maintenance
    Що означає закінчення основної підтримки SAP Business Suite 7 у 2027 році — варіанти Extended Maintenance та стратегічна дорожня карта переходу.
  • 27 жовтня, 15:00 – 16:00
    Navigating the Transition Option for SAP ERP and other SAP Business Suite 7 Products
    Спеціальна хмарна пропозиція для SAP ERP та Business Suite 7 (2031–2033): охоплення, галузеві обмеження та ключові умови хмарного переходу.

SAP Security

  • 6–15 жовтня
    SAP Cybersecurity Month 2026: Security, Compliance & Trust — Are You Ready for What's Next?
    SAP бере участь у Місяці кібербезпеки понад десять років. Цього року — дві тижневі серії відкритих онлайн-сесій для клієнтів і партнерів, присвячені архітектурі безпеки, AI, GRC та управлінню ідентичностями. Реєстрація відкриває доступ до повного розкладу та матеріалів.
  • 15 жовтня, 11:30 – 12:30  або  18:00 – 19:00

Inside SAP

  • 15 жовтня, 16:00 – 17:00
    Accelerating Intelligent Revenue Operations with SAP Sales Cloud & SAP CPQ
    Як SAP будує чисту архітектуру для agentic AI: SAP Sales Cloud, SAP CPQ та SOM/BRIM для автономних операцій з виручкою — від цитування до контракту та провізіонування.
  • 20 жовтня, 16:00 – 17:00
    How SAP runs extended planning & analysis (xP&A) on SAP Analytics Cloud
    SAP повністю перевів фінансове та міжфункціональне планування на SAP Analytics Cloud — стратегія, вибрані use cases та уроки трансформації до agentic-платформи.

SAP Sustainability

    Accelerating Sustainability with AI: From Strategy to Impact
    Штучний інтелект трансформує підхід організацій до сталого розвитку: AI-інсайти оптимізують управління ресурсами, прогнозують екологічний вплив і прискорюють досягнення ESG-цілей.
    Реальні приклади та стратегії інтеграції AI у ваш sustainability-roadmap. Johanna Latt, Sustainability and AI Product Marketing Lead, SAP

entry.title: Jesienny SAP Stammtisch w Katowicach - spotkanie w październiku 2026

Dziękujemy wszystkim uczestnikom za obecność, otwartość i wspólnie spędzony czas. To dzięki Wam nasza społeczność żyje i rozwija się!

Co dalej?

Już dziś zapraszam Was na ostatni w tym roku SAP Stammtisch, który odbędzie się 9 grudnia. W międzyczasie możecie rozważyć ważne eventy SAPowe w których można uczestniczyć wirtualnie!

Jeśli lubicie zdobywać wiedzę, poznawać nowe technologie i być na bieżąco z tym, co dzieje się w świecie SAP, najbliższe tygodnie przynoszą sporo ciekawych możliwości!

Myślę, że każdy znajdzie coś interesującego dla siebie.

Nie możecie pojawić się w Berlinie? Nic straconego! Możecie uczestniczyć online!

👉Rejestracja na SAP TechEd Virtual: https://www.sap.com/events/teched/virtual.html

entry.title: SAP TechEd 2026, mas o que é SAP TechEd?
entry.content:
Olá a todos!

O SAP TechEd 2026 foi oficialmente anunciado e é um evento imperdível para qualquer pessoa que se interesse por tecnologia, inovação e desenvolvimento de sistemas. Para quem ainda é novo neste ecossistema, a SAP é a empresa líder global em software de gestão empresarial, sendo o motor tecnológico por trás das operações das maiores organizações do mundo.

O TechEd é o principal evento focado em tecnologia e desenvolvimento da SAP. É o momento do ano em que a comunidade global se reúne para explorar as mais recentes tendências, desde a Inteligência Artificial até às inovações práticas na transformação de código e arquitetura de dados. É o espaço ideal para nos atualizarmos, partilharmos experiências com outros profissionais e impulsionarmos os nossos projetos atuais.

Para os estudantes universitários que têm a ambição de entrar e crescer na área SAP, este evento é a vossa grande porta de entrada. Participar no TechEd permite-vos ver na prática para onde o mercado de Tecnologias de Informação está a caminhar, proporcionando um contacto direto com soluções de ponta. É uma excelente oportunidade para construir um networking global, ganhar uma visão real das exigências do mercado de trabalho e adicionar um diferencial de enorme peso ao vosso currículo logo no arranque da carreira.

Este ano, o evento vai decorrer de forma presencial em Berlim, mas conta também com uma experiência Virtual muito completa e acessível. Isto significa que todos se podem ligar e aprender com os maiores especialistas da área a partir de qualquer lugar. Vamos inscrever-nos e explorar juntos o futuro da tecnologia?

Todas as informações você pode encontrar em  https://developers.sap.com/teched/

entry.title: Join Me on a Unique Journey: SAP Community and Personal Branding in the Era of AI
entry.content:
Hello everyone!

I would like to share another special SAP Community journey that began recently, and I’m very happy to see that many people are keen to take part in it. I’m referring, of course, to personal branding in the era of AI and how the SAP Community can contribute to it.

Personal branding is not a new topic. I remember hearing about it 20 years ago. But now, together with many other new AI-related opportunities, I believe it has changed significantly.

Before we dive into the details and technicalities, let’s take a step back and see how this journey came about.

My SAP Community Journey

I’ve been with the SAP Community for almost 17 years. As part of my role, I cover many interesting topics. I support SAP Community members as part of my operational activities and responsibilities. I help members engage on the platform, write blog posts, and address issues that come up. The highlight of my day is knowing that I made one more SAP Community member happy. I’m also lucky to engage with the community onsite at events such as SAP TechEd (looking forward to seeing the community at SAP TechEd Berlin 2026!) and SAP Inside Tracks, like SAP Inside Track Porto 2026:

My new community friend Farruk Gillani and myself, exploring the SAP Community together

Over the years, one thing I’ve noticed is that blogging can be challenging for some community members. Sometimes there is a language barrier. Sometimes people simply don’t feel confident enough to contribute, or they feel it takes too much time. Therefore, I’ve always thought about how I can make this whole experience better and easier for members.

Back in 2012, I started Blog It Forward. The basic idea was quite simple: I created a blog post introducing myself using a preset template and then blogged it forward to other people.

People introduced themselves, answered questions, and mentioned others to continue the chain. That also gave people encouragement to participate.

Legacy picture used in the first Blog It Forward post (these are not my real ears, but they belong to the animal featured on the poster behind me. Read below to see how this image relates to the importance of always reviewing AI-generated content).

It was crazy to see how it spread, with almost 300 people participating.

Later, we introduced other initiatives, including Hello SAP Community, which enabled young professionals and students to introduce themselves to the SAP world using simplified blogging. Using a similar approach, we also had the hobby series, where we got to know another, sometimes surprising, side of SAP Community members.

Then came the speaker series. I saw great potential in having speakers engage in the SAP Community around their sessions. We created dedicated templates for speakers, built special series around their content, and helped promote their posts.

With the introduction of AI, another opportunity opened up.

Simplified Blogging Meets AI

Around a year and a half ago, I started incorporating AI into what I call the simplified blogging methodology.

The goal remains the same: make blogging easier and more approachable for people around the world while helping them maintain their unique style and voice.

One approach I used with speakers was very simple: I interviewed them and recorded the conversation. We then had the transcript of that interview, which could be transformed into a blog post structure with the help of AI while keeping the speaker’s authentic voice.

Actually, this blog post itself originated from two main sources: a summary of a session I delivered during Devtoberfest  and a recording of myself talking about the topic while walking.

I love to walk, so recording my thoughts while walking works really well for me. I feel more energized and creative (Blog it Forward was born in a walk in 2012:)).

Me during the walk while recording the majority of this blog post

The process I recommend is quite simple:

  1. Create a template with questions.
  2. Answer those questions naturally.
  3. Record yourself speaking.
  4. Create a transcript.
  5. Ask the AI tool to create a prompt that will help you transform the transcript in to a blog post structure while maintaining your authentic voice, vocabulary, tone, and style. 
  6. Input the prompt, including the relevant transcripts
  7. Review, validate, and improve the result as needed.

For example, your questions could be:

  • Who am I?
  • What am I going to talk about?
  • Why is this topic important to me?
  • What did I learn?
  • What practical tips can I share?
  • What should people be aware of?
  • What is the conclusion from your post?
  • What call to action would you like to end your post with?

The questions already give you the basic structure of the blog post. Instead of sitting in front of an empty page and trying to write everything from scratch, you can simply talk.

AI can then help you with the structure and language.

But this is important: the content should still be yours. Please be sure to read our AI guidelines.

Interesting Anecdote Related to My Image with the Big Ears Above and Why It’s Important to Review AI-Generated Drafts

As I was crafting this blog post, I asked the AI tool which animal was featured on the poster behind me.  It identified these ears as Shrek's ears. These are definitely cool ears! But not Shrek's! This is a small and funny reminder that we should always review. Please share in the comments section below what animal it is:)

Personal Branding in the Era of AI

This brings us back to personal branding. Today, I would like to propose an interesting exercise everyone can try:

Go to your favorite AI tool and ask:

“Who is [your name] +[if needed, add from which company or your topic of expertise]?”

Before you do that, I recommend using a temporary or fresh session rather than your regular conversation history. The idea is to get a result that is less influenced by your previous interactions with the tool.

Look at the answer and take a screenshot. This gives you an interesting starting point for exploring how your personal brand may be represented through AI-generated answers.

From there, you can create a strategy and a plan.

Then work according to the plan, monitor your progress, and adjust it as needed. See what works and what doesn’t work, just as you would with any other project you manage.

For example, I started using “Together we grow” as a theme around my activities and featured it in my LinkedIn profile. Later, I noticed it was reflected in some of the AI results I received.

That was very interesting for me to see.

The Role of SAP Community

Now ask your favorite AI tool another question:

“As an SAP professional, what is the best online site I should engage with to establish and maintain my personal brand as an SAP professional?”

The answers I get usually suggest a combination of SAP Community and LinkedIn: SAP Community for sharing knowledge, demonstrating your expertise, and helping your peers, and LinkedIn for sharing career milestones and expanding your professional network. Of course, other platforms, such as YouTube, can also be considered depending on your personal branding strategy and goals.

This connects directly to something I’ve believed in for many years: sharing knowledge and engaging with others can help you build your personal brand. SAP Community gives SAP professionals a place to share and exchange knowledge, get inspired by each other, ask and answer questions, participate in discussions, find events, follow topics, and publish blog posts. Now, more than ever, being active in the SAP Community will be seen and acknowledged in unique and new ways  

Using AI While Remaining Authentic

When using AI for community contributions:

  • Be transparent about using AI to help create content.
  • Review and validate AI-assisted content before publishing.
  • Add original value rather than posting raw AI-generated output.
  • Take ownership of everything you publish. Your name is on it.

When writing a blog post

  • Write for your audience. Use language and examples that make sense to them.
  • Keep it clear and concise. Use short paragraphs, descriptive headings, and simple language.
  • Give readers something useful. Share insights, lessons learned, practical experience, or actionable tips.
  • Stay authentic and consistent. Write in your own voice, even when AI helps you get there.

Please also read the SAP Community AI guidelines and be sure to follow them.

What Else Can AI Help With?

Transforming a transcript into a blog post is only one possibility.

AI can also help brainstorm ideas.

For example, you might say:

“I’m interested in writing a blog post about Joule Studio. My target audience is beginners. Please suggest topics I could explore.”

Once your blog post is ready, you can also challenge the content, check for areas that need further validation, and look for ideas on how to develop it further.

Another interesting exercise is to check whether the concept you want to write about has already been covered extensively and consider what new value or personal experience you can bring to the discussion.

The important part is that AI supports your contribution rather than replacing it.

Answering Questions Is Also Personal Branding

Blogging isn’t the only way to engage and build your personal brand. Answering questions is another great way. If a question isn’t clear, start by asking the person to clarify it.

When answering, stay focused on solving the original problem. Try to provide insights based on your knowledge and experience rather than simply repeating information that someone could generate themselves with an AI tool. This is where your own experience becomes particularly valuable.

My own journey started many years before today’s AI tools existed. From Blog It Forward to Hello SAP Community, the hobby series, the speaker series, simplified blogging, and now the exploration of personal branding in the era of AI, the common idea has remained quite simple:

Together we grow.

So I invite you to start your own journey by introducing yourself. You can also watch recordings of the two sessions I delivered for more insights to help you doing so:

1) SAP Inside Track Porto (starting 00:31)

2) Devetoberfest Session  

Take a snapshot of where you are today. Think about where you want to go. Engage with the SAP Community. Share your knowledge. Experiment with AI to make contributing easier, but keep your authentic voice and take ownership of what you publish.

Let's end the post with an exciting experiment!

Now, please introduce yourself and share what you learn along the way in the comments section below! See if and how your activities impact your online personal brand.

Let's continue spreading community magic together!✨✨✨

entry.title: 【EventPreview】SAP TechEd Berlin 2026：行く前にカタログを全部数えてみた／Counting Every Session Before I Go
entry.content:
（※English version is available in the latter half of this article.）

※免責事項

本稿は JSUG テクニカル部会のオピニオンリーダーとしての個人の見解であり、JSUG の公式な見解ではありません。セッションの集計と文章の一部には生成AIを使っています。内容の正確性は保証できませんので、情報の活用はご自身の判断でお願いします。

この記事のポイント

  • SAP TechEd Berlin 2026（308件）と ASUG Tech Connect 2026（176件）の公開セッションカタログを、参加前に全件数えてみました。
  • どちらも主役は AI エージェントです（セッションの4〜5割）。TechEd では、AI を「作る」トラックより「設計・運用・保護する」トラックのほうが大きく、全社の AI ガバナンスも独立したトラックになっています。
  • 5月の Sapphire で発表された Joule Work、SAP AI Agent Hub、Joule Studio などは、TechEd ではハンズオンや顧客の話として出てきます。一方で、Anthropic や NVIDIA の名前はカタログに出てきません。
  • ASUG は、移行・費用・ガバナンス・規制の比率が TechEd の2〜3倍です。TechEd は「移行を AI で速くする」、ASUG は「AI のために足元を整える」という向きで、SAP の Christian Klein 氏と ASUG の Geoff Scott 氏の最近の発言もそれぞれ同じ方向を指しています。
  • 現地で見てきたことは、12月8日の JSUG Conference と、1月に予定しているテクニカル部会でお届けします。

はじめに

10月27日から29日まで、ベルリンで SAP TechEd が開かれます。その1週間後、11月2日から4日には米国フォートワースで ASUG Tech Connect があります。JSUG テクニカル部会からは、今年も両方にメンバーが参加します。私はベルリンに行きます。

昨年は ASUG Tech Connect に参加したあとでレポートを書きました。今年は、行く前に書いてみることにしました。

きっかけは出発前の下調べです。どの回に出るかを決めようと公開のセッションカタログを眺めていたのですが、数が多くて目では追いきれません。そこで 、TechEd と ASUG Tech Connect のカタログを全件取得し、形式・トラック・キーワードで数えてみました。すると、一覧を眺めているだけでは気づかなかった傾向がいくつか見えてきました。

これから参加する方、オンラインで見る予定の方、今年は見送る方にも、全体をつかむ材料になればと思ってまとめておきます。数字はすべて10月6日時点の公開カタログによるものです。

1. おさらい：SAP のイベントの位置づけ

ご存じの方も多いと思いますが、簡単におさらいしておきます。SAP が自ら主催する大きなイベントは、今は次の3つです。

  • SAP Sapphire（5月）：経営と事業の発表。オーランド会場は ASUG の年次大会と合同です
  • SAP Connect（10月）：業務部門向け。人事・調達・財務などの大会を、2025年に1つにまとめたものです
  • SAP TechEd（10月）：IT と技術者向け

TechEd には地域版（TechEd on Tour）があり、北米では ASUG Tech Connect がその役割を担っています。日本向けには SAP ジャパンによるオンラインの SAP TechEd Japan があり、JSUG ではメンバーが現地に行って、JSUG Conference等 で報告しています。

2. 今年の流れ：5月に構想、10月に提供開始、そして技術の中身へ

今年の SAP は、5月の Sapphire で「自律型企業（Autonomous Enterprise）」と SAP Business AI Platform を打ち出しました。50以上のアシスタントと200以上のエージェントという構想が示されています。

10月上旬の SAP Connect では、その仕組みの一般提供が始まることが発表されました。ただし、個別のアシスタントの多くは2026年末から2027年初めにかけての提供予定です。

その流れで迎えるのが今回の TechEd です。経営向けに語られた構想が、技術者向けにはどういう中身として語られるのか。今年はそこを見る回だと思っています。

【📷 図1：fig1-event-flow.png／SAP's 2026 event flow from Sapphire to the JSUG Technical SIG】

 

 

3. Sapphire の発表は、TechEd でどう形になっているか

5月の Sapphire で発表されたものが TechEd でどう扱われているかを、カタログで追ってみました。発表の段階だったものが、ハンズオンや顧客の話として出てきています。

  • Joule Work：Sapphire で紹介された、Joule を中心にした新しい作業画面です。TechEd では25件のセッションに登場し、デスクトップ・モバイル・Web で動かすハンズオン（JW163・JW164・JW261）があります。JW206 では、製造・小売・企業 IT で本番運用している顧客の話が紹介されるようです。
  • SAP AI Agent Hub：Sapphire で「7〜9月に提供」とされたエージェントの台帳です。TechEd では、エージェントの発見から廃止までを試すハンズオン（BT161）と、SAP 自身が社内でどう使っているかの回（BT116）が並びます。
  • Joule Studio：51件と、いちばん多く登場します。自分でエージェントを作るハンズオンが複数あるほか、SAP Build から Joule Studio への移行の進め方（AD106）や、移行を準備している製造業 Knapp の話（ST126）もあります。
  • Joule のアシスタント：調達（AS264 Sourcing Assistant）や決算（AS260 Financial Closing Assistant）のアシスタントを実際に触れるハンズオンがあります。
  • SAP Business Data Cloud：データをコピーせずに共有するハンズオン（DA162）や、Henkel で SAP と Adobe のエージェントが連携する事例（DA206）があります。

一方で、Sapphire で大きく取り上げられた外部のパートナー、Anthropic（Claude）と NVIDIA の名前は、TechEd のカタログには一度も出てきません。Databricks も4件だけです。カタログに書かれていないだけで中身として扱われないとは限りませんが、TechEd では「SAP の製品として何ができるか」に話が集中しているように見えます。

4. TechEd Berlin 2026 のカタログを数えてみた

TechEd Berlin のセッションは308件あります。

まず感じたのは、主役がはっきりしていることです。タイトルか概要に AI エージェントが出てくるセッションは144件、全体の47%でした。製品名で多いのも SAP Business AI Platform、Joule、Joule Studio です。

意外だったのはトラックの構成です。9本あるトラックのうち最大は「Architect, operate, and secure AI at scale（AI の設計・運用・保護）」で57件。エージェントやアプリを「作る」トラック（49件）より多いのです。さらに「Drive AI governance for enterprise-wide impact（全社の AI ガバナンス）」が独立したトラックとして27件あります。中身を見ると、エージェントの台帳（SAP AI Agent Hub）、監視（SAP Cloud ALM）、SAP 自身の社内での運用事例などが並んでいます。AI を作る話から、作ったものをどう管理するかの話へ、重心が少しずつ移ってきているように見えます。

【📷 図2：fig2-teched-tracks.png／Sessions per track at SAP TechEd Berlin 2026】

 

一方で、気になった点もあります。

  • 規制（EU AI 法など）に触れるセッションはほとんどありません。ガバナンスは主に、台帳・監視・費用・廃止といった運用管理として語られています。
  • 登壇者の区分が付いた244件のうち232件が SAP です。TechEd のカタログは「SAP が何を打ち出しているか」の地図として読むのがよさそうです。

ちなみに、基盤の呼び名も変わりつつあります。TechEd のカタログでは「SAP Business AI Platform」が41件、「BTP」は1件だけでした。

5. ASUG Tech Connect と比べると

ASUG Tech Connect 2026 のセッションは176件です（公式には190以上とされ、毎週追加されています）。そのうち44件は TechEd と同じ題目の再演です。

主題が AI エージェントなのは同じです。違うのは、その周りの関心でした。

題材 TechEd（308件） ASUG（176件）

AI エージェント47%42%
移行（RISE・移行・転換）7%20%
費用・ROI・価値7%18%
ガバナンス10%18%
規制・コンプライアンス5%11%
クリーンコア3%9%
呼び名「BTP」1件22件
呼び名「Business AI Platform」41件13件

（タイトルと概要文に出てくる語で数えたもので、講演の中身そのものではありません）

【📷 図3：fig3-teched-vs-asug.png／Share of sessions by topic, SAP TechEd Berlin vs. ASUG Tech Connect】

 

移行、費用対効果、ガバナンス、規制の比率は、ASUG のほうが2〜3倍高くなっています。顧客の立場の登壇や顧客事例の回も42件あり、食品・消費財の事例も目立ちます。呼び名も、利用者の側ではまだ「BTP」のほうが通じているようです。

昨年 ASUG に参加したときの感覚とも重なるのですが、TechEd が SAP からの「提供側の地図」だとすると、ASUG は「利用側の悩みの地図」に近いと感じます。同じ AI エージェントの話でも、TechEd は「何ができるか」、ASUG は「どう移行して、いくらかかって、どう管理するか」に寄っています。

6. Clean Core と S/4HANA 移行はどう扱われているか

AI エージェント一色に見えるカタログですが、Clean Core や S/4HANA（SAP Cloud ERP）への移行の話がなくなったわけではありません。TechEd には「Accelerate and de-risk transformation（移行・変革）」というトラックがあり、35件あります。

TechEd で目につくのは、移行の作業そのものに AI を使う回です。たとえば次のような回があります。

  • TM105「Agent-led custom code migration: From planning to mass adaptation」（アドオンの移行をエージェントで進める）
  • TM263「AI-accelerated RISE with SAP migration with the system transition workbench」（ハンズオン）
  • TM108「The journey with clean core continues for SAP Cloud ERP Private」
  • XP110「Beyond migration: Turning Neo sunset into strategic platform transformation」（Neo 環境の終了への対応）

ASUG のほうは顧客事例が中心で、どちらかというと「AI を本格的に使うには、まず Clean Core とデータを整える」という順番で語られています。HP・Jabil・Bristol Myers Squibb が登壇する「AI at Scale Starts with a Clean Core」、Florida Crystals が4週間で Clean Core の評価をした事例、Costco の移行の自動化、Hershey の RISE と Business Data Cloud の事例などです。上の表でも、移行の比率は TechEd の7%に対して ASUG は20%、クリーンコアは3%に対して9%でした。

TechEd は「移行を AI で速くする」、ASUG は「AI のために足元を整える」。同じ Clean Core と AI の組み合わせを、提供側と利用側が逆の向きから語っているように見えます。昨年の記事でも Clean Core は両イベントに共通するテーマでしたが、今年は AI と組になって語られるようになっています。

【📷 図4：fig4-opposite-directions.png／Clean core and AI approached from opposite directions at TechEd and ASUG】

 

7. 両トップの最近の発言も、同じ方向を指している

カタログの傾向は、SAP と ASUG のトップの最近の発言とも重なります。

SAP の Christian Klein 氏は、5月の Sapphire の基調講演で、公開データで学習した汎用の LLM だけでは基幹業務には足りないと述べています。消費者向けの AI なら8割の正確さでも許されるが企業ではそうはいかない、という趣旨で、「Eighty percent is just not good enough」と表現しました。データのモデルが壊れていれば、どんなエージェントでも補えない、とも話しています。10月の SAP Connect の記者会見では、文脈（コンテキスト）とガバナンスはセットだと強調し、3年がかりの移行の時代は終わったとも語ったと報じられています。TechEd で AI の運用と保護のトラックが最大になり、Knowledge Graph の回や移行を AI で進める回が並んでいるのは、この方針がそのまま技術の中身になったものと読めます。

一方、昨年の記事でも紹介した ASUG の Geoff Scott 氏は、10月に公開された ASUG の S/4HANA 調査の紹介で、会員の関心は「S/4HANA に移ること」から「S/4HANA で価値を出すこと」に移り、定着やガバナンス、稼働後の取り組みに向いていると話しています。8月のインタビューでは、エージェントは整ったデータに頼るので、顧客や品目をどう定義するかといったマスターデータのガバナンスを、判断を任せる前に決めておく必要があると指摘しました。今は実験することが何より大事だ、とも述べています。ASUG のカタログで移行・費用・ガバナンスの比率が高く、「AI のためにまず足元を整える」顧客事例が並ぶのと、ちょうど同じ向きです。

面白いのは、二人とも「データと文脈とガバナンスが先」という点では一致していることです。違うのはその先で、SAP は「だから SAP の基盤とクラウドで」、ASUG は「だから、まず自分たちのデータを整えよう」と続きます。TechEd と ASUG の違いは、この立ち位置の違いがそのまま出たものなのかもしれません。

8. 日本の会社は登場するか

少し気になって、登壇者の所属も調べてみました。TechEd Berlin では、登壇者（延べ675人）の所属に日本企業は見当たりませんでした。

ASUG Tech Connect では、日本にゆかりのある会社の米国拠点の事例が2つあります。DIC グループの Sun Chemical による API のモダナイゼーションと SAP BTP の事例と、2019年にパナソニックから独立した i-PRO Americas による受注処理の自動化の事例です。i-PRO の回の紹介文には、日本のチームも関心を持っていると書かれています。

ちなみに5月の Sapphire（オーランド）には、ダイキン、富士通、武田薬品などの事例があり、SuccessFactors の基調講演にはトヨタの方も登壇していました。経営と事業の場である Sapphire には日本企業の名前が出てくるのに、技術の場ではまだ少ない。日本のユーザーが技術の話をする側に回れるとよいな、と思います。

9. 私が現地で見てきたいこと

ここからは個人の関心です。私は AI を作る話よりも、作ったものを企業としてどう管理するかに関心があります。今年はちょうど、そこが TechEd の大きな柱になっているので楽しみにしています。具体的には、次のようなことを確かめてきたいと思っています。

  • エージェントの台帳と統制は、SAP 以外のエージェントまでどこまで見られるのか
  • AI の使用量に応じた課金（AI ユニット）は、利用者からどう見えて、どう管理できるのか
  • 移行やアドオンの書き換えをエージェントに任せる話は、実際にどこまで使える段階なのか

ハンズオンでは、AI を使ったサイバーレジリエンスの机上演習（XP160）と、SAP Company Memory のプレビュー（BT162）に参加する予定です。

おわりに

カタログの数字は、あくまで「何が予定されているか」です。会場で実際に何が語られ、参加者が何に反応しているかは、行ってみないと分かりません。

持ち帰った情報のお届けについて

現地で見聞きしたことは、次の2つの場でお届けする予定です。

  • 12月8日（火）JSUG Conference 2026：テクニカル部会のセッション「B-2 SAP最新技術情報の共有～TechEd・ASUG Tech Connect 2026より～」（11:15〜12:00）で、TechEd と ASUG Tech Connect に参加したメンバーが現地の最新情報をお届けします。
    お申し込みはこちら：https://www.jsug.org/conference2026
  • 1月のテクニカル部会：参加したメンバーが、それぞれのテーマをより詳しく紹介します。日程と申込方法は決まりしだい、この記事に追記します。開催後の資料の配布先も、あわせてここでお知らせする予定です。

どちらも JSUG の会員の方であればご参加いただけます。詳細は JSUG のホームページをご覧ください。

この記事で書いたのは、あくまで行く前の「読み」です。実際に確かめてどうだったのか、予想どおりだったところも外れたところも、両方の場で正直にお伝えしたいと思います。ぜひご参加ください。

TechEd は同じ日程でオンライン（SAP TechEd Virtual）でも基調講演と一部のセッションが配信されます。今年は現地に行かない方も、ぜひのぞいてみてください。ベルリンでお会いできる方がいれば、声をかけていただけるとうれしいです。

データについて

  • SAP TechEd Berlin 2026 公式セッションカタログ、ASUG Tech Connect 2026 公式アジェンダ（いずれも2026年10月6日に取得・ログイン不要の公開情報）
  • どちらのカタログも、内容が変わる可能性があると明記しています

[English Version]

Before SAP TechEd Berlin 2026: What I Learned by Counting Every Session in the Catalog

Disclaimer:

This article reflects my personal views as an Opinion Leader of the JSUG Technical SIG and does not represent the official views of JSUG. Generative AI was used to compile the session data and to draft parts of the text. I cannot guarantee the accuracy of the content, so please use the information at your own discretion.

Key points

  • Before attending, I counted every session in the public catalogs of SAP TechEd Berlin 2026 (308 sessions) and ASUG Tech Connect 2026 (176 sessions).
  • AI agents are the main theme of both events (40–50% of sessions). At TechEd, the track on architecting, operating, and securing AI is larger than the track on building agents and apps, and enterprise-wide AI governance has its own track.
  • Joule Work, SAP AI Agent Hub, Joule Studio, and other announcements from SAP Sapphire in May now appear at TechEd as hands-on workshops and customer stories. Anthropic and NVIDIA, however, are not mentioned in the TechEd catalog.
  • At ASUG, migration, cost, governance, and regulation come up two to three times more often than at TechEd. TechEd leans toward "using AI to speed up migration," while ASUG leans toward "getting your foundation ready for AI." Recent remarks by SAP's Christian Klein and ASUG's Geoff Scott point in the same respective directions.
  • What we learn on site will be shared at the JSUG Conference on December 8 and at the JSUG Technical SIG meeting planned for January.

Introduction

SAP TechEd takes place in Berlin from October 27 to 29. A week later, from November 2 to 4, ASUG Tech Connect is held in Fort Worth, Texas. As in previous years, members of the JSUG (Japan SAP Users' Group) Technical SIG will attend both events. I will be going to Berlin.

Last year, I wrote a report after attending ASUG Tech Connect. This year, I decided to write something before I go.

It started as preparation for the trip. I was looking through the public session catalogs to decide which sessions to attend, but there were simply too many to follow by eye. I collected every session from the TechEd and ASUG Tech Connect catalogs and counted them by format, track, and keyword. A few trends emerged that I would not have noticed just by scrolling through the lists.

I hope this gives a useful overview to those attending, those watching online, and those skipping this year. All figures are based on the public catalogs as of October 6.

1. A quick recap: SAP's major events

Many readers will already know this, but here is a brief recap. SAP currently hosts three major events of its own:

  • SAP Sapphire (May): Strategy and business announcements. The Orlando event is held jointly with the ASUG Annual Conference.
  • SAP Connect (October): For line-of-business users. It brought together the separate events for HR, procurement, finance, and other areas into one in 2025.
  • SAP TechEd (October): For IT professionals and technologists.

TechEd also has regional editions (TechEd on Tour), and in North America ASUG Tech Connect plays that role. In Japan, SAP Japan holds the online SAP TechEd Japan, and JSUG sends members to the events and reports back at the JSUG Conference or etc.

2. This year's flow: vision in May, availability in October, then the technical details

At Sapphire in May, SAP introduced the "Autonomous Enterprise" and the SAP Business AI Platform, with a vision of more than 50 assistants and more than 200 agents.

At SAP Connect in early October, SAP announced that general availability of these capabilities is starting. Many of the individual assistants, however, are planned for late 2026 to early 2027.

TechEd comes next in this flow. I see this year's TechEd as the place to find out what the vision presented to executives looks like in technical terms.

【📷 Figure 1：fig1-event-flow.png】

 

3. How Sapphire announcements are taking shape at TechEd

I used the catalog to trace how the Sapphire announcements appear at TechEd. Things that were announcements in May now show up as hands-on workshops and customer stories.

  • Joule Work: The new Joule-centered workspace introduced at Sapphire. It appears in 25 TechEd sessions, including hands-on workshops on the desktop, mobile, and web experiences (JW163, JW164, JW261). JW206 is described as featuring customers who run it in production in manufacturing, retail, and enterprise IT.
  • SAP AI Agent Hub: The agent inventory that Sapphire said would be available in Q3. TechEd offers a hands-on workshop covering agents from discovery to decommissioning (BT161) and a session on how SAP uses it internally (BT116).
  • Joule Studio: The most frequent, appearing in 51 sessions. There are several hands-on workshops for building your own agents, a session on the transition path from SAP Build to Joule Studio (AD106), and a story from the manufacturer Knapp, which is preparing for that transition (ST126).
  • Joule assistants: Hands-on workshops let you try assistants for sourcing (AS264, Sourcing Assistant) and financial closing (AS260, Financial Closing Assistant).
  • SAP Business Data Cloud: A hands-on workshop on sharing data products without copies (DA162) and a Henkel case in which SAP and Adobe agents work together (DA206).

On the other hand, Anthropic (Claude) and NVIDIA, the external partners highlighted at Sapphire, are not mentioned anywhere in the TechEd catalog, and Databricks appears only four times. Not being in the catalog does not mean they will not be covered, but TechEd seems to focus on what SAP's own products can do.

4. Counting the SAP TechEd Berlin 2026 catalog

TechEd Berlin has 308 sessions.

The first thing I noticed is how clear the main theme is. AI agents appear in the title or abstract of 144 sessions, or 47% of the total. The most frequent products are SAP Business AI Platform, Joule, and Joule Studio.

What surprised me was the track structure. Of the nine tracks, the largest is "Architect, operate, and secure AI at scale" with 57 sessions, more than the track for building agents, workflows, and applications (49). "Drive AI governance for enterprise-wide impact" is also a separate track with 27 sessions. Looking inside, you find the agent inventory (SAP AI Agent Hub), monitoring (SAP Cloud ALM), and SAP's own internal operations. The center of gravity seems to be shifting gradually from building AI to managing what has been built.

【📷 Figure 2：fig2-teched-tracks.png】

 

A few points also caught my attention:

  • Very few sessions mention regulation (such as the EU AI Act). Governance is mostly discussed as operational management: inventory, monitoring, cost, and decommissioning.
  • Of the 244 sessions with a speaker type, 232 are SAP. It makes sense to read the TechEd catalog as a map of what SAP is promoting.

By the way, the platform name is also changing. In the TechEd catalog, "SAP Business AI Platform" appears in 41 sessions and "BTP" in only one.

5. Compared with ASUG Tech Connect

ASUG Tech Connect 2026 has 176 sessions (officially 190+, with more added every week). Of these, 44 are repeats with the same titles as TechEd sessions.

AI agents are the main theme here too. The difference is in the surrounding interests.

Topic TechEd (308) ASUG (176)

AI agents47%42%
Migration (RISE, migration, conversion)7%20%
Cost, ROI, value7%18%
Governance10%18%
Regulation, compliance5%11%
Clean core3%9%
Name "BTP"122
Name "Business AI Platform"4113

(Counted by words in titles and abstracts, not by the actual content of the talks.)

【📷 Figure 3：fig3-teched-vs-asug.png】

 

Migration, ROI, governance, and regulation appear two to three times more often at ASUG. There are also 42 sessions with customer speakers or in the customer story format, with many food and consumer goods cases. On the user side, "BTP" still seems to be the more familiar name.

This matches my impression from attending ASUG last year: if TechEd is SAP's "map of what is offered," ASUG is closer to a "map of what users are struggling with." Even on the same topic of AI agents, TechEd leans toward what is possible, and ASUG leans toward how to migrate, how much it costs, and how to manage it.

6. Clean core and S/4HANA migration

The catalogs may look as if they are all about AI agents, but clean core and migration to S/4HANA (SAP Cloud ERP) have not gone away. TechEd has a track called "Accelerate and de-risk transformation" with 35 sessions.

What stands out at TechEd are sessions that use AI for the migration work itself. For example:

  • TM105 "Agent-led custom code migration: From planning to mass adaptation"
  • TM263 "AI-accelerated RISE with SAP migration with the system transition workbench" (hands-on)
  • TM108 "The journey with clean core continues for SAP Cloud ERP Private"
  • XP110 "Beyond migration: Turning Neo sunset into strategic platform transformation"

ASUG is built around customer stories, and the order tends to be "to use AI at scale, first get your clean core and data in shape." Examples include "AI at Scale Starts with a Clean Core" with speakers from HP, Jabil, and Bristol Myers Squibb, Florida Crystals' four-week clean core assessment, Costco's migration automation, and Hershey's RISE and Business Data Cloud journey. In the table above, migration is 7% at TechEd versus 20% at ASUG, and clean core is 3% versus 9%.

TechEd says "use AI to speed up migration," and ASUG says "get your foundation ready for AI." The provider side and the user side seem to approach the same combination of clean core and AI from opposite directions. In last year's article, clean core was a common theme of both events; this year, it is discussed together with AI.

【📷 Figure 4：fig4-opposite-directions.png】

 

7. Recent remarks by both leaders point the same way

The catalog trends also match recent remarks by the leaders of SAP and ASUG.

In his Sapphire keynote in May, SAP's Christian Klein said that general-purpose LLMs trained on public data are not enough for mission-critical business. Consumer AI may get away with 80% accuracy, but businesses cannot, as he put it: "Eighty percent is just not good enough." He also said that no agent can make up for a broken data model. At the SAP Connect press Q&A in October, he reportedly stressed that context and governance go together and declared the end of three-year migrations. The fact that the AI operations and security track is the largest at TechEd, alongside sessions on the Knowledge Graph and AI-driven migration, can be read as this direction turning into technical content.

Meanwhile, ASUG's Geoff Scott, whom I also quoted in last year's article, said in October, when ASUG's S/4HANA research was published, that members' attention has shifted from getting to S/4HANA to getting value from it, with a focus on adoption, governance, and post-go-live work. In an interview in August, he pointed out that agents depend on clean, consistent data, so companies need to decide how to govern master data, such as how to define a customer or a product, before they hand decisions over to agents. He also said that experimenting is the most important thing right now. This fits well with the higher share of migration, cost, and governance in the ASUG catalog and its customer stories about getting the foundation ready for AI.

What I find interesting is that both agree that data, context, and governance come first. The difference is what follows. SAP continues with "so use SAP's platform and the cloud," while ASUG continues with "so let's get our own data in order first." The difference between TechEd and ASUG may simply reflect this difference in standpoint.

8. Do Japanese companies appear?

Out of curiosity, I also checked the speakers' companies. At TechEd Berlin, I found no Japanese companies among the speakers (675 speaker slots in total).

At ASUG Tech Connect, there are two sessions from US operations of companies with Japanese roots: Sun Chemical, part of the DIC Group, on API modernization and SAP BTP, and i-PRO Americas, which became independent from Panasonic in 2019, on automating order processing. The i-PRO session description mentions that its team in Japan is also interested.

By contrast, Sapphire Orlando in May included cases from Daikin, Fujitsu, and Takeda, and a speaker from Toyota appeared in the SuccessFactors keynote. Japanese companies show up at Sapphire, the business-focused event, but are still rare at the technical events. I hope more Japanese users will take the stage to talk about technology.

9. What I want to see on site

This part is my personal interest. I am more interested in how companies manage AI than in how they build it. This year, that happens to be one of TechEd's main pillars, so I am looking forward to it. Specifically, I want to find out:

  • How far the agent inventory and governance can see, including non-SAP agents
  • How usage-based pricing for AI (AI Units) looks to users and how it can be managed
  • How ready, in practice, it is to hand migration and custom code rework over to agents

For hands-on workshops, I plan to join the AI-enabled tabletop exercise for cyber resilience (XP160) and the SAP Company Memory preview (BT162).

Closing

The numbers in the catalog only show what is planned. What is actually said on stage and what attendees react to can only be seen on site.

Sharing what we bring back

We plan to share what we see and hear at the following two events:

  • JSUG Conference 2026, Tuesday, December 8: In the Technical SIG session "B-2: Sharing the Latest SAP Technology Updates from SAP TechEd and ASUG Tech Connect 2026" (11:15–12:00, in Japanese), members who attended TechEd and ASUG Tech Connect will share the latest information from the events.
    Registration: https://www.jsug.org/conference2026
  • JSUG Technical SIG meeting in January: Attending members will cover their topics in more detail. I will add the date and registration information to this article once they are announced, along with a link to the materials after the meeting.

Both events are open to JSUG members. Please see the JSUG website for details.

What I wrote here is only my reading before the event. I want to share honestly at both events what turned out as expected and what did not. I hope you can join us.

TechEd keynotes and some sessions will also be streamed online on the same dates (SAP TechEd Virtual), so please take a look even if you are not going this year. If you will be in Berlin, I would be happy if you said hello.

  • Both catalogs state that their content is subject to change
  • This article compiles and organizes public information and does not represent the official views of SAP or ASUG

entry.title: Know an SAP Champion: My Conversation with Mustafa Bensan about AI at SIT Porto 2026
entry.content:
At SAP Inside Track Porto 2026, one session stood out for me: Mustafa Bensan’s presentation on SAP’s Autonomous Enterprise vision. After the session, I took the chance to introduce myself and talk with him about AI.


With SAP Champion Mustafa Bensan at SAP Inside Track Porto 2026

Who is Mustafa?

Mustafa is an SAP Champion and the founder and Chief Architect of Intentum, with more than 30 years of experience on SAP projects around the world. What I found encouraging is that he started his career as an ERP functional consultant, like many of us, before moving into analytics and architecture.

What impressed me in his session

Mustafa’s presentation went into much more detail, including a full live demo. Here I’m sharing just a few points that stood out to me as a finance consultant.

The highlight was a live voice demo. Mustafa simply spoke to an AI voice agent, and the agent responded to him in real time. No searching for transaction codes, no navigating through screens: you speak, and you get an answer.

The voice agent was built on the LiveKit platform, and the demo was inspired by SAP’s partnership announcement with LiveKit at SAP Sapphire Madrid. Seeing it live made the idea of the “Autonomous Enterprise” feel much less abstract. Instead of users having to know where to look in the system, they can simply ask.

What we talked about

After the session, we talked about where AI is heading in SAP and what it means for the people who work with these systems every day. For me, it was valuable to hear the perspective of someone who has seen so many technology shifts in SAP over three decades.

What it meant to me

As an SAP FICO and Joint Venture Accounting consultant, my first thought was about finance. If a user can simply ask a question and get an answer, finance work like checking balances, investigating postings or preparing for the month-end close could become much faster, especially for business users who don’t know every report and transaction code.

But in finance, an answer is only useful if it’s correct and you can trace where it came from. Finance teams are rightly careful about where their data goes and where their numbers come from. So for me, the key questions for any AI assistant in finance are: which data does it use, how is that data secured, and can the user verify the answer?

That’s where finance consultants continue to play an important role: making sure the data behind the answers is right, that the right controls are in place, and that users know how to check what they’re told.

My takeaway

I came away more curious than worried. Conversational AI will change how we work with SAP, and I want to understand it early, especially how it can support finance processes in a trusted and controlled way.

Thank you, @MustafaBensan , for taking the time to talk with me, for a session that made the future of SAP feel very real, and for kindly clarifying the details of the demo afterwards. And to anyone attending an SAP event: don’t hesitate to approach an SAP Champion. One short conversation can give you a lot to think about.

#KnowAChampion #CatchAChampion #SAPCommunity #SAPChampions

entry.title: HighRadius vs. SAP FSCM: Hard-Earned Lessons from a Global Cosmetics S/4HANA Transformation
entry.content:
As consumer goods and beauty organizations accelerate their digital finance transformations, the debate surrounding Accounts Receivable (AR) optimization often gets reduced to a binary question: Should we use native SAP Financial Supply Chain Management (FSCM) or replace it with a specialized cloud solution like HighRadius? Over an 18-year career leading global SAP transformations across Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, I have watched finance executives repeatedly fall into the trap of treating this as an "either/or" software selection choice.

The reality on the ground is completely different. When you move past the product brochures and slide decks, you discover that the most successful global templates do not choose between them. Instead, they treat SAP as the core transactional engine and HighRadius as an intelligent edge layer. Achieving this coexistence, however, requires navigating complex architectural integration points, version-specific database behaviors, and industry-specific commercial nuances—such as complex trade promotions and massive retail deductions—that software vendors rarely mention during the sales cycle.

The Friction Point: Why Pure SAP FSCM Fell Short in Global Beauty & Cosmetics Rollouts

To understand where native capabilities hit their limits, we can look at a global cosmetics leader's rollout running on an SAP S/4HANA 2023 On-Premises environment with Feature Package Stack 02 (FPS02). The business model managed a deeply fragmented customer landscape: massive multinational retail networks (such as Sephora, Ulta, and major department stores), thousands of highly localized salon accounts, and high-volume e-commerce payment clearing.

Initially, the steering committee pushed for a pure SAP FSCM Collections and Dispute Management implementation to minimize their software footprint and leverage their existing licensing. However, as we entered the blueprinting and prototyping phases, the operational limitations of a purely rule-based system in the cosmetics industry became apparent:

  • The Trade Promotion Deduction Avalanche: Major retail beauty chains routinely short-pay invoices based on cooperative advertising agreements, volume rebates, and markdown allowances. In standard SAP FSCM, these deductions flood the subledger as individual residual open items. Dispute specialists spent up to 40% of their day manually linking these short payments to promotional agreements, creating a massive operational backlog.
  • Static Collection Strategies: SAP FSCM generates collection worklists based on static, pre-defined rules—such as aging buckets, risk categories, and total open values. In a fast-moving retail consumer landscape, these rigid rules created bottlenecks. The system flooded collection specialists with alerts for large, stable retail accounts that routinely paid according to strict corporate payment cycles, while high-risk, deteriorating independent salon behaviors slipped through unnoticed because they hadn't crossed a specific net-due threshold.
  • The Analytics Deficit: Standard SAP operational reporting (even via custom operational data provisioning views or standard Fiori FES 2023 apps) provided lagging operational KPIs. The business leadership lacked predictive cash forecasting and granular, dynamic Day Sales Outstanding (DSO) trend analysis segmented by shifting channel behavior patterns (D2C vs. B2B Wholesale).

The organization realized that while FSCM was perfectly engineered to maintain the financial integrity of the ledger, it lacked the algorithmic agility needed to optimize cash application hit rates and automatically resolve multi-brand deduction claims. This realization shifted our strategy to a hybrid architecture deploying the HighRadius Cash Application Cloud and Deduction Management System (DMS) modules alongside our SAP core.

Architectural Reality: Orchestrating Integration via Hyperion Integration Platform (HIP)

Integrating a multi-entity S/4HANA 2023 core with a cloud-based Autonomous Finance platform is rarely a "plug-and-play" exercise. For this transformation, we built a hybrid ecosystem where SAP functioned strictly as the immutable system of record, while HighRadius operated as the system of engagement and intelligence, orchestrated via the Hyperion Integration Platform (HIP) as the corporate middleware layer.

The underlying architecture relied on standardizing data exchange protocols across an enterprise footprint. Because the corporate landscape utilized HIP as its centralized enterprise middleware, we funneled all transactional deltas, ledger extract files, and incoming bank lockbox information through this layer to perform essential schema transformations before delivering them to High Radius.

The technical complexity surfaced heavily during the orchestration of the data loop between HighRadius Cash App, DMS, and SAP FI-AR via HIP:

  1. The Cash App Ingestion: HighRadius Cash App automatically extracts unstructured remittance data via OCR from customer emails and retail vendor portals, matching payments against open customer line items. This open item subledger data is periodically extracted from SAP operational views (such as BSID) and delivered through HIP as a structured outbound file payload.
  2. The DMS Splitting Mechanism: When a retail client short-pays an invoice due to a trade promotion dispute, the Cash App module flags the variance and automatically routes the residual shortage amount to the HighRadius DMS module.
  3. Automated Inbound Postings through HIP: Once a deduction is classified in the cloud, HighRadius communicates the clearing parameters back down. HIP intercepts this response payload, translates the cloud parameters into SAP-compatible structures, and executes an inbound transactional interface leveraging standard functions like BAPI_ACC_DOCUMENT_POST. This automatically clears the original invoice line item in S/4HANA, posts a residual open item for the short-payment, and maps specific SAP Reason Codes corresponding to the dispute type (e.g., Pricing, Shortage, or Coop Ad).

By utilizing HIP as the unified integration layer, we eliminated complex point-to-point interface sprawl, ensuring that our daily cash application cycle remained decoupled from the extended timelines required to research and settle retail trade promotions.

Version Constraints and Unexpected Implementation Roadblocks

Moving from conceptual architecture to actual deployment on S/4HANA 2023 (FPS02) exposed several technical constraints that project planners frequently overlook.

Our first major hurdle involved the Universal Journal (ACDOCA). In older SAP ERP Central Component (ECC) environments, financial data was highly segmented across index tables (like BSID and BSAD). S/4HANA’s unified ACDOCA design vastly speeds up internal reporting, but extracting massive delta datasets of open and cleared items to feed external machine learning models can degrade system performance if not carefully managed.

During initial data cycles, our delta extraction queries for historical customer payment behaviors began causing severe memory bottlenecks in the SAP HANA database due to the sheer volume of line items generated by cosmetic wholesale shipments. We had to configure the SAP extraction jobs and HIP to abandon generic open-ended queries and completely redesign our extraction logic. We restricted data pulls to strict timestamp-based delta captures leveraging specialized SAP Change Data Capture (CDC) mechanisms, ensuring that data replication to HighRadius occurred in controlled micro-batches outside of peak financial closing windows.

Another critical constraint appeared within the Business Partner (BP) master data synchronization. Because this was a global program spanning multiple geographies and brands, the client utilized complex BP groupings with varying field modification rules across different company codes. HighRadius requires a highly standardized payload for its ingestion models.

We encountered repeated integration errors where localized fields in SAP (such as specific regional tax classification rules or localized payment block reasons) caused data validation rejections in the HighRadius staging tables. This required a comprehensive data-cleansing initiative and configuring specialized transformation rules within HIP to map heterogeneous SAP BP attributes into a unified schema that the HighRadius machine learning algorithms could accurately interpret.

The Measurable Bottom Line: Concrete Project Outcomes

The true validation of this hybrid architectural strategy lies in the quantifiable business results achieved in 12 months of post-go-live. By shifting from static, rule-based workflows to an AI-driven, predictive model, the global shared services organization transformed its balance sheet performance:

 

The dramatic leap in our auto-cash application hit rate was particularly impactful for the consumer goods model. By leveraging HighRadius’s OCR and machine learning algorithms to automatically parse unstructured remittance advices from customer emails and retail vendor portals, the system matched payments to open items in S/4HANA without human intervention. This freed up our senior credit analysts to focus exclusively on negotiating complex promotional shortages rather than manual data entry.

Strategic Recommendations for Enterprise Architects Today

If I were to approach a global cosmetics architecture rollout again today, I would change my implementation strategy in two distinct areas:

  1. Mandate Early-Stage Data Cleansing: Do not wait for the integration testing phase to discover that your SAP Business Partner master data or customer hierarchies are inconsistent across regions. Master data remediation must be treated as a strict technical prerequisite that runs six months before any external cloud integration work begins.
  2. Enforce the Transactional Boundaries Immediately: Be incredibly disciplined about keeping business logic where it belongs. Cloud platforms will tempt you to build complex custom validation workflows or store trade promotion contracts within their environments. Resist this pressure. All accounting principles, credit limits, and final clearing rules must reside strictly within the S/4HANA core to protect your financial system of record. Use the HIP-enabled cloud edge purely for execution speed, prediction, and user experience.

Ultimately, the choice between SAP FSCM and HighRadius is a false dichotomy. The real challenge—and the real opportunity for enterprise architects—lies in configuring a robust, high-performing integration framework that respects the transactional authority of SAP while fully unleashing the analytical power of autonomous finance.

Author Bio

Prakashreddy Bodireddy is an SAP S/4HANA Certified FICO Solution Architect with 18+ years of experience delivering global finance transformation programs across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia, and the Americas. His expertise includes SAP S/4HANA Finance, FSCM,  Group Reporting, IFRS15/RAR, Treasury, and HighRadius integration.

Hello SAP Community!

I’m Fatemeh Zarei, and I’ve been working with the SAP Community team for over a year now, creating content and helping share stories from across the community.

During this time, I’ve had the opportunity to attend D-COM and SAP Inside Track Hamburg. Attending SAP Inside Track Hamburg gave me the opportunity to enjoy interesting sessions and connect with fellow community members. I’ve always loved events for exactly this reason: the chance to exchange ideas and get to know the people behind the technology. That experience helped me better understand SAP technology and connect with the great SAP community in Hamburg.

That’s also why I enjoy hearing people’s stories after an event. We can attend the same event and come away with completely different experiences. A session you almost skipped might become your biggest takeaway, or a quick conversation might introduce you to someone you’ll stay connected with.

So, why not share your upcoming SAP TechEd Berlin experience with the SAP Community?

You don’t need to be an experienced blogger, and you don’t need to write about everything that happened. A few highlights, useful lessons, or memorable community moments are a great place to start.

Let’s go!

Your SAP TechEd Story: 10 Questions to Get You Started

Use some of the questions below as a starting point for your blog post draft. Choose the ones that are meaningful to you, skip the others, and add anything else you’d like to share.

Who are you, and what brought you to SAP TechEd?

Introduce yourself briefly. Tell readers about your role, your interests, and whether this was your first SAP TechEd.

What were you most looking forward to, and how did the experience compare?

Perhaps you wanted to explore a particular technology, get hands-on experience, or meet fellow community members. Tell us how it went and what surprised you.

Which session stood out to you, and why?

Share what made it worth attending and your main takeaway. Include a link to the session or related resources so readers can explore further.

What technology or idea are you excited to explore further?

Whether it’s SAP Business AI, Joule, application development, integration, or something completely different, tell us what caught your attention and why.

What did you learn that you could apply in your work?

Describe a practical tip, a new approach, or an idea you’d like to try with your colleagues, customers, or projects.

Did a session or conversation change your perspective?

Tell us what you thought before and what made you see things differently. It could be a technical insight or something you learned from another person’s experience.

Who did you connect with, and what made that interaction memorable?

Maybe you met someone you previously knew only online, reconnected with a community friend, or had an unexpected conversation. Share what made that connection special and tag the people you met so they can join the conversation. If you took a picture together, consider including it, with their permission of course 🙂

What was your favorite SAP TechEd moment?

Choose one moment that captures the event for you. If you have a picture, include it and tell us the story behind it: what was happening, who you were with, and why it mattered.

What advice would you give a first-time attendee?

Share a practical tip you wish you’d known beforehand—whether it’s about choosing sessions, preparing for the event, or making time for community activities.

What comes next?

Tell us what you plan to do with what you learned. You might try a new technology, share your takeaways with colleagues, stay in touch with someone you met, or create your next SAP Community contribution.

Now It’s Your Turn! ✨

Your blog post doesn’t have to follow this exact order or answer all ten questions. Choose the ones that help you tell your story and add pictures and useful links along the way.

Before publishing, complete the Tour the SAP Community tutorial if you haven’t already, it’s required for blogging and will help you get familiar with the platform before sharing your story.

Ready to share? Create your blog post in Community Corner and add the SAP TechEd and SAP Community tags so others can find your story.

Finish by inviting readers to join the conversation. You could ask: “What was your biggest SAP TechEd takeaway?”

Most of all, write in your own voice. Your experience and perspective are what make your contribution worth reading.

I’m looking forward to reading your SAP TechEd stories and discovering the sessions, people, and moments that made the event special for you!

Have fun blogging!

Curious about using AI agents in your ABAP development workflow? SAP Expert Thomas Alexander Ritter introduces a major update to SAP’s official ABAP development tools MCP server. With its own read and edit tools, the server now works with CLI tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Codex without depending on the tools provided by VS Code chat. Explore the post for an overview of its architecture, features, and guidance on getting started.
